newsitem.title: USA: Sluggish US cash crudes lose balance, grades even.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish US cash crudes lose balance, grades even.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes lost ground late Thursday in-line with technical selling on the NYMEX market, while domestic grade barrels hardly budged.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing is trading around 35 cents lower at $19.80-90 a barrel, around 4-5 cts higher than second month July.
Cash markets lacked headlines to excite price direction, and foreign crude activity, along with domestics, were stilted by low volumes and little talk.
Industry gatherings kept many players out of their offices, leaving dealings unmoved.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at 7 cts and 8 cts under the benchmark, steady to only a shade weaker than Wednesday. Concerns over wide WTI/Brent spreads pressured prices, traders said.
West Texas Sour/Midland was pegged at a $1.75 discount to the marker, again slightly weaker than Wednesday.
Sours were pressured by talk of Iraqi Basrah Light on offer in the U.S. Gulf, at $2.20-25 under June WTI for July 1 arrival.
Other grades hardly were mentioned, with WTI/Cushing Postings around $1.80-85.
U.N. sanctions on Iraq were maintained earlier Thursday at the Security Council's regular 60-day review.
The action has become routine procedure, as Baghdad continues to conceal weapons of mass destruction, according to U.N. Special Commission inspectors.
Maintaining broad sanctions against Iraq is not related to the oil-for-food accord, which will come for renewal ahead of the June 7 end for the six-month deal.
